gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-gentium-plus: Bold and expressive, Balsamiq Sans draws every stroke like bent cable, with no pinched curves anywhere. And Gentium Plus follows in the classic serif role, its wide-mouthed c giving the lowercase a refined, settled look.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-gowun-batang: Balsamiq Sans moves in one unbroken, stencil-like line throughout. Gowun Batang, a text serif with terminals cut back to leave generous gaps, gives a longer passage a refined, literary hush that the heading never tries for.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-habibi: Balsamiq Sans bends its strokes like cable, never swelling or thinning. It handles the loud, expressive work, while Habibi, a traditional text serif with a clear channel leading into each round letter, does the quieter editorial job of carrying sentences.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-inika: Inika is a traditional text serif with a see-through gap in each s. Balsamiq Sans earns its keep when it runs big and short, its technical-pen line staying bold and expressive.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-kay-pho-du: Balsamiq Sans lays down bold, expressive lines with the constant weight of a stencil-cut channel. Kay Pho Du supplies the counterweight: a traditional serif whose breathing counters and rolling-ball strokes make the pair feel like two eras sharing a page.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-laila: Laila reads as an editorial text serif, leaving generous space between its curve ends and the stem. Balsamiq Sans is best at shouting in one bold, uniform line, while Laila is best at settling in.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-montaga: Montaga reads bookish and editorial, its pen-lifted curves leaving loops pleasantly unfinished. Balsamiq Sans, by contrast, keeps its stroke uniform as stencil-cut channel, so a longer passage in the text serif feels like a hush after a shout.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-new-tegomin: New Tegomin reads dignified and traditional, its c a wide-open ring. Balsamiq Sans is best at bold, expressive display lines with no hairlines at all, while New Tegomin is best at quiet, serious text.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-podkova: Podkova reads bookish and traditional, its c opening broad and welcoming. Balsamiq Sans brings the opposite energy, strokes pulled like solder through a nozzle, and that clash of bold and bookish is the pair's strongest quality.
gen-gf-balsamiq-sans-gf-rhodium-libre: Balsamiq Sans bends wire-like s curves that never thin at the spine, bold and expressive from the first word. But Rhodium Libre, a classic serif with brush ends lifted before each curve closes, is the one built to carry editorial text.
